title: Promptset compatibility checklist and action journal — week of 2026-06-18
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight weekly check-in focused on promptset compatibility and the most actionable regressions we found while onboarding new model variants (v2q, v3-compact) into the hosted inference catalog. Purpose is to produce a short checklist for release engineers and a prioritized action journal for applied-ml to follow up on before next rollout.

Top-line summary (short):
- Overall regression rate across promptsets: 6.4% (up from 4.9% last week).
- Most common failure motif: hallucinated facts in instruction-following tasks (45% of regressions).
- Highest-severity buckets: formatting regressions that break downstream parsers (10% of regressions) and hallucination on regulatory promptsets (3 incidents flagged).
- Immediate blockers for rollout: one promptset failing schema validation (payments-parsing-pset) and a latency anomaly on v3-compact under short-seq inference (90th percentile jump from 120ms -> 220ms).

Quick metrics snapshot (how we measured):
- Baseline sample: 12 promptsets selected from onboarding pool (mix of QA, shopping, code, regulatory).
- Runs: 1000 prompts per set, mix of deterministic sampling + temperature variations.
- Regression definition: any output that (a) deviates from golden label in eval suite AND/OR (b) triggers a downstream parser error.
- Alerts raised: 6 (auto-created tickets), triage severity distribution: P0=1, P1=3, P2=2.

Failure motifs (examples & rough counts):
1) Fact hallucination (55/120 regressions)
   - Example: prompt "List the current CEO of AcmeCorp"
     - expected: "Jordan Lee"
     - v3-compact: "Jordan Li" + added fabricated detail about tenure.
   - Hypothesis: tokenization + quantization on v3-compact amplifies preference for surface-level name variants; confidence calibration off for named-entity completions.

2) Format/schema break (12/120 regressions) — high impact
   - Example: payments-parsing-pset expects JSON with fields {amount, currency, payee}
     - expected: valid JSON
     - v2q: returned bare text "Paid $10 to X" causing parser crash in downstream flow.
   - Immediate risk: blocks dedicated customers ingesting parser output raw.

3) Instruction collapse / prompt-echo (30/120)
   - Example: few-shot instruction prompts lose step bulleting; model returns single paragraph. Affects retrieval-augmented flows where step delimitation matters.

Observations (notes to self):
- Regression distribution skews by prompt length: short prompts (<=12 tokens) show more format errors; medium prompts see hallucination.
- v3-compact shows modest quality drop on code generation style tests but improves latency and cost — good trade, but need targeted prompt tweaks.
- Some false positives in auto-eval: fuzzy-match threshold too strict for paraphrase-tolerant promptsets (increase similarity threshold for those sets).

Promptset compatibility checklist (for release engineers):
- [ ] Run schema validation harness on every promptset runner (payments-parsing-pset flagged).
- [ ] Include 50 short-form prompts (<=12 tok) in the smoke suite for v2q/v3-compact.
- [ ] Add named-entity slot-checker to catch subtle NER hallucinations during onboarding.
- [ ] Bake in parser-safe fallback (if output fails JSON parse, return structured error with trace id).
- [ ] Re-run latency profile under short sequence distribution and capture 95/99 percentiles (Riley).

Action journal (owners & deadlines):
- Payments parser failure triage — owner: Priya Kapoor — due: 2026-06-21 — details: reproduce, attach failing prompts, create minimal reproduction job with streaming disabled. (JIRA-ML-4221 linked)
- Short-seq latency spike investigation — owner: Riley Chen — due: 2026-06-20 — notes: compare kernel selection logs between v2q and v3-compact; check batching behavior under low-queue conditions.
- NER slot-checker PoC — owner: Miguel Santos — due: 2026-06-25 — produce lightweight ner-checker that flags token-level substitutions with confidence delta.
- Eval fuzzy-threshold adjustments — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2026-06-22 — experiment on 3 promptsets to calibrate similarity metric; update runner config.
- Canary config: enforce parser-safe fallback on 10% of traffic for the next week — owner: release-oncall — due: 2026-06-19.

Notable triage notes (short bullets):
- Payments-parsing-pset failure: reproducible on v2q with seed=42. Repro script saved under /infra/onboard-repros/payments-v2q-42 (internal path note).
- One regulatory prompt produced verbatim PII from training tokens in v3-compact — flagged for research/privileged-review.
- Onboard eval harness currently lacks streaming-off mode in some runners; can produce different outputs (TODO: unify runtime flags across runners).

Hypotheses and quick experiments (what to try next):
1) Hypothesis: quantized attention kernel in v2q increases token-ambiguous NER substitutions. Experiment: run NER probing suite with and without quantized kernel (A/B). Metric: NER substitution rate per 1000 tokens.
2) Hypothesis: short-seq latency spike is due to fallback to CPU for some kv-cache ops; Experiment: capture device placement logs for the hot path on v3-compact.
3) Quick mitigation: add post-output sanitizer to enforce JSON schema or else inject stable error token — cheap and deployable as edge transform.

Examples to paste into tickets (copy-paste friendly):
- "Input: "{\"text\": \"Paid $10 to Acme\"}"
  v2q output: "Paid $10 to Acme"
  downstream: JSONParseError at parser.py:84
  Severity: P1"

- "Input: "Who is the CEO of AcmeCorp?"
  v3-compact output: "Jordan Li, appointed 2010, previously CTO at BetaCo"
  Expected: "Jordan Lee"
  Severity: P2 (hallucination, regulatory risk for finance prompts)"

Meeting sync & next steps:
- Triage huddle: 2026-06-19 10:00AM PT — quick 20m stand to assign blocks and confirm repros.
- Follow-up deep-dive: 2026-06-22 2:00PM PT — owners present results from experiments and propose rollback/canary plan if quality thresholds unmet.

Open questions (brainstorm style):
- Should we add a dedicated "schema-fail" metric to the cost dashboard? (helps link economic impact to regressions).
- Is the threshold for hallucination alerts too permissive for news-type prompts? How to adapt per-promptset?

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Save current eval runner logs and attach to JIRA-ML-4221 (done: logs uploaded, mark in ticket).
- Draft short-run checklist for release engineers -> convert to template in Confluence.
- Re-run the short-form smoke suite after the NER PoC lands.

Appendix (mini-runbook snippets):
- If parser crash observed: insert traffic-split fallback (10% safe mode) and set incident severity P1 until fix validated.
- If hallucination on named entities > 30% of prompts: escalate to research for calibration; consider prompt-engineered slotting as temporary mitigation.

End of journal entry — comments welcome.

(If you're scanning this quickly: prioritize payments-parsing-pset repro and short-seq latency spike investigations.)
